scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1 and V1"; Phase 3 "Depends on: Phase 2 and V2"; Phase 4 "Depends on: Phase 3 and V4; V6"
scores.rationale: Phases go from schema/tokenization to defenses to features to model to enforcement, with each gated on a validation gate and an explicit dependency map.

scores.evidence: A real authorization from an allow-listed internal test or employee card at a real merchant... The switch logs the response and ignores it
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real production end-to-end slice across 7 tiers with deploy, rollback and a trace.

scores.evidence: Fail open: fall back to existing rules plus network score... Flip condition: V3 fails, or measured fraud during fail-open windows exceeds the risk owner's limit
scores.rationale: The gates table gives reversibility, default, assumption, validator and flip condition for every irreversible decision, and the assumptions are labeled.

scores.evidence: Phase 5: "Enforcement rollout (exposure smallest first)"; Phase 2 puts circuit breaker and kill switch before widening 1%→10%→100%
scores.rationale: Within phases, the widest-impact items (schema freeze, defenses, kill switch) come before leaf work. Rollouts go from the smallest exposure to the widest.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "PAN stays in the switch; mTLS; segmented namespace; secrets in Vault; card allow-list"
scores.rationale: The per-phase table has concrete security content in every phase 0–6, starting with the first phase.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "One OpenTelemetry trace across all tiers; latency and timeout alerts; logs hold tokens only"
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Terraform and ArgoCD; signed images"; Phase 4: "MLflow: data snapshot, code hash, hyperparameters, feature version"
scores.rationale: Reproducibility has concrete content in each phase: IaC, schema versions, a shared feature library, snapshot IDs and deterministic retraining.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Timeout plus fail open; rollback by flag"; Phase 2: "Circuit breaker; kill switch; store recovery drill (RTO)"
scores.rationale: Failure handling and rollback appear in every phase, starting with Phase 0 fault injection.

scores.evidence: Guardrail defense, cost+latency budget and human-in-the-loop are built in Phase 2; retrieval 3, model access 4, memory, orchestration 3–4, routing 6, feedback 1/6
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human-in-the-loop come before the capabilities, and the rest follow the required order. Feedback capture starting early is a justified exception (E1) with its own constraints.

scores.evidence: Decommissioning the existing rules engine. Pull forward when: two quarters at 100% enforcement pass V7.
scores.rationale: The plan lists several deferred items, each with a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: This plan is very strong on every dimension. It has a production walking skeleton, up-front gates with flip conditions, security, observability, reproducibility and resilience threaded through each phase, and a justified feedback-early exception.
